## Purpose

`batch_patient_profiles()` renders patient profiles to PDF files, without running a DaVinci application, so they
can be distributed or archived. It takes the same configuration as `mod_patient_profile()`, described in the
[Patient Profile Module](a00-papo.html) article, and the data must meet the same
[data requirements](a01-data_requirements.html).

## Usage

Rendering requires pandoc, a LaTeX distribution with `xelatex`, and the DejaVu Sans Mono font.

```{r}
library(dv.papo)

batch_patient_profiles(
  subjid_vals = list(
    review_A = c("01-701-1015", "01-701-1023"),
    review_B = "01-701-1028"
  ),
  dataset_list = dv.papo:::prep_safety_data(n = 5), # demo data
  subject_level_dataset_name = "adsl",
  subjid_var = "USUBJID",
  summary = list(vars = c("SITEID", "AGE", "SEX"), column_count = 3),
  listings = list("Adverse Events" = list(dataset = "adae")),
  output_dir = "profiles"
)
```

Each element of `subjid_vals` becomes a PDF named after it, so this writes `review_A.pdf` (two subjects) and
`review_B.pdf` (one subject) to `profiles/`, plus `manifest.csv`, which records whether each was rendered. An
element that fails gets a `<name>.txt` error report instead of a PDF, and the others are still rendered. Existing
files are never overwritten: the call stops if any of its output files already exists.

Unlike the module, the PDF is static:

- the summary is a single-row table: `column_count` is still required, but ignored;
- listings show the `default_vars` columns, or all columns if it is not set;
- value plots draw one plot for each of their `default_analysis_params`, and none if it is not set.

See `?batch_patient_profiles` for the other arguments.
